THIRD-PARTY RUST CRATES
=======================

This file lists the Rust crates linked into bin\birelate-server.exe, with the licence texts
of every crate LICENSE does not cover. It is generated by tools/rust-licenses.py: the
normal-dependency closure of birelate-server from `cargo metadata` for target
x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, intersected with `cargo tree -p birelate-server -e normal`
(build scripts, build-dependencies and dev-dependencies are excluded). Procedural-macro
crates (serde_derive and the like) are part of that closure and are listed and marked, but
they run only at build time and are not linked into the binary. Where a crate vendors C/C++
sources (the *-sys crates), the licence files found in those sources are included too.
Crates that do not ship their own licence file are marked below. Where their licence requires a
copyright notice (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0), the text printed here is the LICENSE of the crate's
upstream repository at the commit the crate was published from, and the entry's `notice` line
gives the file; if the repository has no licence text, it is the standard text with the
copyright line from the repository's notice file or, failing that, the crate's authors field,
and the entry says so. Of an OR licence the MIT text is given. For the rest (public-domain
dedications such as CC0-1.0) the licence expression from the crate's manifest is the only
licence information available here.

525 third-party crates, 7 MIT OR Apache-2.0 Koharu crates, 333 distinct licence texts.

(MIT OR Apache-2.0).

   for more information.

   “Combinatorial Modeling of Chromatin Features Quantitatively Predicts DNA
   Replication Timing in _Drosophila_” by Federico Comoglio and Renato Paro,
   which is licensed under the CC-BY license. See
   http://www.ploscompbiol.org/static/license for more ifnormation.

 - alice29.txt, asyoulik.txt, plrabn12.txt and lcet10.txt are from Project
   Gutenberg. The first three have expired copyrights and are in the public
   domain; the latter does not have expired copyright, but is still in the
   public domain according to the license information
   (http://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/53).
